messages:
maria: heads-up - nightly CI shows a perf + correctness regression in the long-seq Flash variant when we allow dtype promotion to fp8/bf16. small heads-up repro below.

arjun: ugh, can you paste the failing CI log? which kernel exactly?

maria: flashx-paged fallback toggling between fused-flash and paged-flash for seq_len 4096+ on A100 (driver 510). we see softmax spikes and occasional large logits -> NaNs after an fp8 cast step.

maria: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T02:01:12Z] kernel_select: picked fused-flash (kw: fused_flash_v2)
[2026-03-17T02:01:12Z] perf: latency 12.8ms -> 47.3ms after kernel switch
[2026-03-17T02:01:13Z] numeric: softmax pre-scale max=1.2e4 mean=23.4
[2026-03-17T02:01:13Z] cast(fp8): clipped values > 1e3 -> infs
[2026-03-17T02:01:13Z] output: NaN detected in logits
```

sophie: repro command? I want to run on my local dev box.

maria: easy: `python -m bench.attn_run --model t5-large --seq 4096 --batch 2 --enable-fp8 --kernels fused_flash,paged_flash --kv-page 1`

patrick: quick notes: 1) kernel selector has hysteresis set to 0 (immediate flip) 2) batching heuristic will merge short+long sequences into same batch which trigs a different kernel path 3) fp8 quant path currently uses a shared scale per-batch, no per-head clamp.

chen: thinking out loud - softmax overflow usually occurs when logits are extremely unbalanced; fp8 quant/rounding could push things over. Did we recently change the softmax pre-scale?

maria: yes - recent perf change to avoid an extra cast removed a small logit-scale clamp in the bf16-to-fp8 path. seemed harmless in microbenchmarks.

arjun: temporary mitigation: add a cheap clamp before fp8 cast: `clamp_logits = torch.clamp(logits, min=-1e3, max=1e3)` then resume kernel. Does that stop NaNs in CI?

bench-bot: benchmark run queued (id=br-92345) using clamp_logits workaround. ETA ~6m.

ops-bot: deployed a canary patch to the kernel-selector config: added 200ms hysteresis window for kernel swaps on nodes with >32GB cache pressure.

maria: ran local with clamp -> no NaNs, perf hit ~+3% for seq4096 but stable.

sophie: can we do a smarter adaptive clamp instead of a fixed 1e3? maybe per-head stddev based: scale = max(1, stddev*6) then clamp at mean +/- scale*max_scale. keeps head-sensitive.

patrick: idea: keep kernel selection deterministic per-request shape + dtype. don't let batching combine shapes that cause kernel flip in the hot path. add a pre-batching normalization step that groups by (seq_bucket, dtype, kv_paged).

chen: also important: when we promote to fp8 we should compute a fallback score: if max_abs(logits)/median_abs > threshold then bypass fp8 path for that batch. cheap check.

arjun: agree. action items:
- add clamp/fallback check in fp8 conversion (maria)
- add per-shape hysteresis in kernel selector to avoid flip-flops (patrick)
- update batching heuristic to not mix long/short sequences where possible (patrick + ops)
- add targeted test in nightly that simulates KV cache page churn with mixed batches (sophie)

maria: i'll open PR for clamp + repro test now. will also attach the exact failing sample and seed.

maria: attaching the minimal failing prompt in the PR: `seed=1729 prompt=repeat('x', 4096)`

bench-bot: br-92345 completed: clamp workaround eliminated NaNs; perf delta: fused-flash path +2.8% latency, memory unchanged. fallbacks triggered in ~0.6% of batches.

ops-bot: leaving canary enabled for 3 hours, rolling back if error rate > 0.5% or if latency > +10%.

patrick: long-term: we should add a numeric-safety hook in the runtime that runs an inexpensive statistic on logits distribution post-attn and tags bad batches for rerun with safer kernels. This could be enabled per-customer.

chen: filing a follow-up RFC to formalize fp8 safety nets + per-head scaling.

maria: thanks all. will link PR and CI after green. cc @arjun @patrick @sophie
